text:
A: Hiya! Oh, there you are. I'm Tracey, nice to meet you, hun.
B: Hiya. Joanne.
A: Joanne, lovely. Where are you?
B: St Helens.
A: Oh, near Liverpool, isn't it? I'm Chelmsford, Essex. Sorry, I'm in the kitchen, I've just come back from my morning class, so excuse the gym top. I teach spin, circuits, that sort of thing. The six o'clock was full again today, I've got a waiting list for it now, which is mad for six in the morning, isn't it?
B: Six in the morning. No thanks.
A: Ha! That's what everyone says, and then they come and they're hooked. What about you, what do you do?
B: I'm a carer. For me mum. She's got dementia.
A: Oh, babe, I'm sorry. That's a lot.
B: It's alright. It's what you do, isn't it.
A: It is, to be fair. Does she live with you?
B: No, four streets away. I'm round there most of the day. Then back for Gary's tea.
A: That's full-on. Do you get any time for yourself? Because honestly, I say this to my clients, you can't pour from an empty cup, you know?
B: I go for a walk in the park, mornings.
A: Oh, that's good, that's really good. Walking's underrated. I do Parkrun in Chelmsford a couple of times a month, I did the London Marathon a few years back, and it's not even about the fitness, it's your head, isn't it? Clears it.
B: I just walk round. I'm not running.
A: No, no, I'm not saying run. Walking's perfect.
B: Right.
A: So, erm, has she been diagnosed long, your mum?
B: Three years. I gave up work for it. Warehouse.
A: Oh wow. See, that's a big thing to do. I don't know if I could, to be honest. My mum's on her own in Basildon since my dad died and I don't get over there half as much as I should. It's always the A12, or I've got clients, or Callum needs something. There's always an excuse, isn't there?
B: Yeah. There is.
A: Sorry, that sounded bad.
B: No, it's just honest. My sister's the same. She's in Warrington, twenty minutes away, and I still do all of it.
A: Oh, that would do my head in. Have you said anything?
B: Not really. We don't talk much now.
A: Families, eh. Right, okay. Do you get out at all, nights out, anything?
B: No. I'm not a night out person.
A: Not even a little meal? I'm out with the girls most weekends, we do an Italian in Brentwood. I'm off to Marbella in the summer as well, already booked it.
B: We used to go to Prestatyn. Caravan.
A: Oh, lovely, bit of sea air.
B: It was alright. Not been since me mum got ill.
A: Well, you deserve a break, honestly. Even one night. Is there anyone who could pop in?
B: Not really, no. I'd only worry.
A: Yeah, I get that. I'd be the same with...
